summary: Recess and physical education are scheduled, measured, and unequally distributed — the schools serving the most Black children offer the least of both in the federal data. The recess file.

title: Black Accountants: Inside the Profession With the Two-Percent Problem
summary: Accounting is America's language of money, and its credentialed ranks are about two percent Black — a figure so famous it has a name inside the profession. The CPA file.

title: Sepsis: The Emergency That Finds Black Patients Younger, Sicker, and Later
summary: Black Americans develop sepsis at higher rates, at younger ages, and die of it more — a disparity the hospital data trace from the infection's first hour to the ICU door.

title: The Repair Shop: Wrenches, Trust, and the Last Trade You Can't Offshore
summary: Auto repair is America's archetypal skilled-trade business — local, physical, trust-based — and Black shop owners hold a working share of it as the EV era rewires the trade. The repair file.

title: Black Population in Montana: The Bicycle Corps and the Smallest Map
summary: About 13,000 Black Montana residents — one in eighty — the smallest share in the nation, with a history written by Buffalo Soldiers. The census profile.

title: Black Rochester: Douglass's City After Kodak
summary: Rochester holds about 85,000 Black residents in the city — two-fifths — and 170,000 across the metro. The census profile.

title: The Summer File: Where the Gap Actually Grows
summary: The most replicated finding in the achievement literature is a calendar: the gaps grow over the summers, not the school years. The summer file reads the evidence and the programs answering it.

title: The Clergy: Ministry as Work in Black America
summary: The Black church is one of the largest employers in Black America — and its pastors are among its most bivocational, least pensioned workers. The clergy file.

title: Cataracts: The Curable Blindness That Waits Longer in Black Eyes
summary: Cataract surgery is among medicine's most successful procedures — and Black Americans receive it later and less, carrying more avoidable vision loss in the Medicare data.

title: The Print Shop: Ink, Institutions, and the Paper Trail of Black America
summary: The Black print shop printed the movement's leaflets, the church's programs, and the funeral's obituaries — a small industry with an outsized archive. The printing file.

title: Black Population in Idaho: River Street and the Boise Resettlement Hub
summary: About 32,000 Black Idaho residents — one in fifty-seven — between Boise's historic River Street and a refugee hub's new generation. The census profile.

title: Black Syracuse: The 15th Ward's Ground Beneath the Viaduct
summary: Syracuse holds about 45,000 Black residents in the city — nearly a third — and 85,000 across the metro. The census profile.

title: Twenty-Two or Fifteen: The Class-Size Evidence
summary: American education ran one true experiment on class size, in Tennessee — and its largest gains belonged to Black children in small rooms. The class-size file.

title: The Forecasters: Black Meteorologists and the Science America Watches
summary: The broadcast meteorologist is the most-watched scientist in America — and the weather enterprise behind the forecast is about three percent Black. The meteorology file.

title: Peripheral Artery Disease: The Circulation Gap Measured in Limbs
summary: Black Americans with blocked leg arteries face amputation at rates up to four times higher — and receive flow-restoring procedures less — in the vascular surgery data.

title: The Appraisers: The Small Profession That Decides What Every Home Is Worth
summary: Fewer than one in a hundred licensed appraisers is Black — in the profession whose signature sets the value of Black America's largest asset. The appraisal file.

title: Black Population in Wyoming: The Least Populous State's Smallest Community
summary: About 12,000 Black Wyoming residents — one in forty-eight — in the nation's least populous state, rooted in its forts and railroads. The census profile.

title: Black Omaha: North Omaha's Long Arc From the 24th Street Days
summary: Omaha holds about 60,000 Black residents in the city and 95,000 across the metro — Malcolm X's birthplace and the plains' oldest Black community. The census profile.

title: The First Bell: School Start Times and the Sleep Data
summary: Biology says teenagers wake late; the bell schedule says 7:30. The districts that moved the bell produced data — and the gains pooled exactly where this atlas would look. The first bell file.

title: The People Who Drive the City: Black Transit Workers
summary: Public transit runs on Black labor — the operators, mechanics, and station staff of the nation's buses and trains, in a workforce that is the public sector's bluest collar. The transit file.

title: The Emergency Room: The Safety Net's Front Door Opens at Different Speeds
summary: The ER cannot turn anyone away — but Black patients wait longer to be seen, leave unseen more often, and arrive by ambulance to diverted hospitals in the emergency care data.

title: The Staffing Agency: Selling the Bridge Between Workers and Work
summary: Staffing is the business of the match — and Black-owned agencies hold a distinctive franchise in the warehouses, hospitals, and offices of their own communities. The staffing file.

title: Black Population in North Dakota: Fargo's New Americans and the Oil Patch
summary: About 42,000 Black North Dakota residents — one in nineteen — in the fastest-transforming small population in the northern plains. The census profile.

title: Black Des Moines: Center Street's Legacy and Iowa's Black Center
summary: Des Moines holds about 25,000 Black residents in the city and 50,000 across the metro — small in count, central in Iowa's Black data. The census profile.

title: The Virtual Classroom: Online Schools in the Outcome Data
summary: Virtual schooling promised to route around every broken building in this atlas. The enrollment surged; the outcome studies are the education file's most lopsided verdict. The virtual file.

title: The Watch: Black Workers in Protective Services
summary: Security guards, corrections-adjacent staff, bailiffs, and screeners: protective services employ Black workers at among the highest rates of any occupation group — at its widest internal divide. The watch file.

title: The Last Care: Hospice, Dying, and the Black Family's Terms
summary: Black Medicare patients use hospice less, enroll later, and die in intensive care more — a gap the research ties to access, information, and a well-earned insistence on fighting. The end-of-life file.

title: The Wedding Industry, Black-Owned: Planners, Venues, and the Jumping Broom Economy
summary: Weddings are a seventy-billion-dollar industry with a Black consumer base it long underserved — and Black vendors have built its most distinctive shelf. The wedding file.

title: Black Population in South Dakota: Sioux Falls and the Lost Boys' Landing
summary: About 32,000 Black South Dakota residents — one in twenty-eight — centered on Sioux Falls, where the 'Lost Boys' of Sudan made their American home. The census profile.

title: Black San Diego: The Southeast and the Navy's City
summary: San Diego holds about 105,000 Black residents in the city and 190,000 across the metro — a military-built community in America's finest-weather city. The census profile.

title: The Robotics Team: After-School STEM in the Participation Data
summary: The build season's robot is the STEM pipeline's most visible machine — and its team rosters reproduce the access map of every other file. The robotics file.

title: The Grounds: Black Landscaping and Groundskeeping Workers
summary: The people who keep America's lawns, campuses, cemeteries, and courses employ Black workers in the hundreds of thousands — outdoors, exposed, and increasingly organized into ownership. The grounds file.

title: The Last Mile of the Prescription: Pharmacy Access and the Adherence Gap
summary: The prescription is written — then the data follow it to the pharmacy counter, where deserts, copays, and closures decide whether the medicine ever gets taken. The pharmacy access file.

title: The Lender's Side of the Desk: Black-Owned Mortgage and Lending Businesses
summary: Every denial-gap article has a mirror image: the Black-owned brokerages and lenders built to work the desk from the other side. The lending file.

title: Black Population in Nevada: The Mountain West's Largest Share
summary: About 385,000 Black Nevada residents — one in eight — the highest Black share of any Mountain West state, built by the Las Vegas economy. The census profile.

title: Black Hartford: The North End, the West Indians, and Bloomfield
summary: Hartford is nearly two-fifths Black in the city — about 45,000 residents — with a Caribbean depth rare in New England. The census profile.

title: The Library File: School Libraries, Librarians, and the Vanishing Den
summary: The school library was the one room that asked nothing and gave everything — and its certified librarians are disappearing first from the schools that hold this file's students. The library file.

title: The Headset Economy: Black Customer-Service Workers
summary: Nearly three million Americans answer the phones, and Black workers are close to a fifth of them — in the occupation now first in line for the algorithm. The headset file.

title: The Recovery Gap: Rehabilitation After the Hospital Saves You
summary: Surviving the stroke or the surgery is the first medicine; rehabilitation is the second — and Black patients are discharged home, instead of to rehab, at measurably higher rates. The recovery file.

title: Feeding the Occasion: Black-Owned Catering Businesses
summary: Catering is the food economy's event wing — and one of Black business's deepest benches, from the church-kitchen graduate to the corporate contract caterer. The catering file.

title: Black Population in Washington: Seattle's Gravity and the Bases
summary: About 490,000 Black Washington residents — one in sixteen — centered on Seattle–Tacoma and the Joint Base Lewis-McChord corridor. The census profile.

title: Black Providence: Fox Point, the Cape Verdeans, and Rhode Island's Capital
summary: Providence holds about 28,000 Black residents in the city and 105,000 across Rhode Island — home to America's Cape Verdean heartland. The census profile.

title: The Backpack File: Black Students in Foster Care
summary: A foster child's school record reads like a travel diary — a new school with every placement, credits lost at every border. Black children are a quarter of the foster system, and its classroom data are the steepest in this section.

title: The Players: Black Athletes as a Workforce
summary: Professional sports are a workplace with the strangest demographics in the employment file: majority-Black labor, a three-year median career, and the most scrutinized wages in America. The players file.

title: The Allergy File: Food Allergies Rising Fastest in Black Children
summary: Food allergies are climbing across America — and fastest, with the least diagnosis and the least epinephrine, among Black children. The allergy file.

title: The Bakery Shelf: Black-Owned Bakeries and the Dessert Economy
summary: From the pound cake's church economy to the cupcake boom and the king cake's seasonal empire, Black bakeries run one of the food business's sweetest ledgers. The bakery file.

title: Black Population in Oregon: The Exclusion State's Long Correction
summary: About 195,000 Black Oregon residents — one in twenty-two — in the only state admitted to the Union with a Black exclusion clause in its constitution. The census profile.

title: Black Albany: Arbor Hill and New York's Capital Region
summary: Albany holds about 29,000 Black residents in the city and 95,000 across the Capital Region — a community older than the republic it now helps govern. The census profile.

title: The Unread Word: Dyslexia, Screening, and the Late Diagnosis
summary: Dyslexia is the most common reading disability on earth — and its diagnosis, in the identification data, arrives latest and least for the Black children whose reading scores need it most. The dyslexia file.

title: The Coal File: Black Miners of Appalachia
summary: Black miners dug a fifth of Appalachia's coal in the industry's prime — recruited, segregated, unionized, and finally stranded by the same seams. The coal file.

title: The Injured Brain: Traumatic Brain Injury's Uneven Map
summary: Traumatic brain injury hospitalizes and kills Black Americans at higher rates — from the playing field to the fall at home — and its long recovery runs through the same gaps as every file here.

title: The Route Economy: Black-Owned Pest Control Businesses
summary: Pest control is the service economy's quiet annuity — a route of monthly stops that compounds. Black owners run a growing shelf of it. The pest control file.

title: Black Children and Youth: The Youngest Fifth of Black America
summary: About 14 million Black Americans are under 18 — a younger population than the nation's, with its own geography, composition, and data. The census profile.

title: Black Durham: The Hayti District and Black Wall Street's Other Home
summary: Durham holds about 95,000 Black residents in the city and 150,000 across its metro — the city that built Black Wall Street beside Tulsa. The census profile.

title: No Fixed Address: Black Students in the Homeless Count
summary: More than a million American students have no fixed address — most of them doubled up in somebody else's home — and Black children are counted among them at twice their share. The address file.

title: The Watermen: Black Oystermen, Crabbers, and Seafood Workers
summary: The Chesapeake and the Gulf were worked for two centuries by Black watermen whose skill fed the nation's oyster houses — and whose industry the water itself is retiring. The watermen file.

title: Sarcoidosis: The Disease That Chose Black Women
summary: Sarcoidosis strikes Black Americans at several times the rate of white Americans, hits Black women hardest, and kills at rates that make it this section's quiet outlier. The sarcoidosis file.

title: Everything They Own: Black-Owned Moving Companies
summary: The moving company holds a family's whole material life in its hands for one day — a trust business built on muscle, logistics, and reputation. The moving file.

title: Black Grandparents and Kinship Care: The Multigenerational Safety Net in the Data
summary: Black grandparents form about a fifth of America's grandparent caregivers from an eighth of the population — the kinship layer of the household data.

title: Black Winston-Salem: Tobacco's Twin City and the Arts School
summary: Winston-Salem holds about 90,000 Black residents in the city and 130,000 across the metro — a tobacco city with an HBCU and an arts identity. The census profile.

title: The Unquiet Mind: ADHD and the Diagnosis That Arrives Late
summary: The symptoms are reported at the same rates; the diagnosis is not. Black children with ADHD are found later, medicated less, and disciplined more for the same neurology. The ADHD file.

title: The Union Card: Black Workers and Organized Labor
summary: Black workers carry union cards at the highest rate of any major group in America — a fact with a century of history and a measurable paycheck inside it. The union file.

title: What's Actually on the Plate: Diet Quality in the Federal Numbers
summary: The government's own diet score gives Black Americans lower marks — while the same data show a food culture whose traditional core outperforms the national diet. The diet quality file.

title: The Flower Shop: Black Florists and the Language of Occasions
summary: Florists arrange the community's whole emotional calendar — the wedding, the homegoing, the apology, the altar — and Black shops have held that corner for generations. The florist file.

title: Black Suburbanization: The Majority Now Lives in the Suburbs
summary: A majority of Black Americans in large metros now live in suburbs — the defining Black geographic shift of the past half-century. The census data.

title: Black Fayetteville: Fort Liberty's City and the Sandhills
summary: Fayetteville holds about 95,000 Black residents in the city and 135,000 across the metro — a community built beside the Army's largest post. The census profile.

title: The Test: Standardized Scores and What They Actually Measure
summary: The score gaps are real, published annually, and argued over eternally. Read closely, the testing data measure a student's resources as faithfully as her reasoning — and the era of the test-optional experiment is now grading the test itself.

title: The Field Hands' Ledger: Black Farmworkers and Agricultural Labor
summary: Before the factory there was the field — and the hired hands who harvested America's food were, for a century, substantially Black. The farm labor file.

title: Strong Bones, Late Charts: The Bone-Health Paradox
summary: Black Americans have the densest bones and the lowest fracture rates in the federal data — and among the worst outcomes when a bone does break. The bone health file.

title: The Developer File: Black-Owned Real Estate Development Firms
summary: Developers decide what gets built and who it is for — and Black firms hold about two percent of that industry, with a pipeline pointed at the neighborhoods that need it most. The developer file.

title: Black Rural America: The Black Belt, the Colonias of the Delta, and the Small Towns
summary: About one in ten Black Americans lives in rural America — concentrated in the Black Belt crescent from Virginia to Texas. The census profile.

title: Black Augusta: The Garden City, the Godfather, and the Medical District
summary: Augusta holds about 105,000 Black residents in the city and 150,000 across the metro — a majority-Black Georgia city with James Brown in its marrow. The census profile.

title: The Lottery: Black Families and the School-Choice Market
summary: The charter lottery is the most democratic admission in American education — and the most consequential gamble many Black families ever take with a child's future. The choice file.

title: The Bridge Workers: Black Interpreters, Translators, and Language Professionals
summary: Every hospital consent and courtroom plea in two languages passes through one workforce — and Black linguists staff the bridges into Creole, Spanish, French, and sign. The bridge file.

title: The Itch in the Data: Eczema and Skin Read on Its Own Terms
summary: Eczema hits Black children harder and is read worse on dark skin by the textbooks that teach it — the dermatology file's training-data problem, measured in rashes. The eczema file.

title: The Daycare on the Corner: Black-Owned Child Care Businesses
summary: America's child care runs substantially out of Black women's homes and storefronts — a licensed, inspected, essential industry priced like a favor. The child care business file.

title: Black Americans with Disabilities: One in Four Adults
summary: About a quarter of Black adults report a disability in the federal health surveys — the intersection of the disability and race data.

title: Black Savannah: The Hostess City's First City of the Georgia Coast
summary: Savannah holds about 88,000 Black residents in the city and 125,000 across the metro — from First African Baptist's 1773 founding to the port's modern cranes. The census profile.

title: The Counselor's Caseload: 400 Students, One Chair
summary: The school counselor is the gatekeeper of every file in this section — the courses, the colleges, the crises — and she carries four hundred students, in schools where the chair is sometimes empty altogether. The counselor file.

title: The Code Keepers: Black Workers in Medical Records, Coding, and Billing
summary: Every diagnosis in America becomes a code, and every code a bill — translated by a back-office workforce of half a million, substantially Black and female. The code keepers' file.

title: The Blood Count: Anemia, Iron, and the Hemoglobin Line
summary: Anemia is diagnosed against a line drawn through a distribution that differs by ancestry — and the argument over where the line belongs is one of laboratory medicine's oldest. The anemia file.

title: The Itinerary File: Black-Owned Travel Agencies and the Black Travel Economy
summary: Black travelers spend well over a hundred billion dollars a year — and the agencies designing those journeys, group by curated group, are substantially Black-owned. The itinerary file.

title: Black LGBTQ Americans: The Williams Institute Population Data
summary: An estimated 1.4 million Black adults identify as LGBTQ in the Williams Institute's data — about one in eight Black adults. The demographic profile.

title: Black Mobile: Alabama's Port City and the Last American Slave Ship
summary: Mobile holds about 95,000 Black residents in the city and 140,000 across the metro — nearly half the city, from Africatown to the shipping channel. The census profile.

title: The Band Room: Marching Bands and the Loudest Pipeline in School
summary: The marching band is the Black school's public orchestra and the HBCU's beating heart — and its first gate is a thousand-dollar instrument in a fifth-grader's hands. The band file.

title: The Lab File: Black Workers in Phlebotomy and the Clinical Laboratory
summary: Every diagnosis in this atlas passed through a tube, a slide, or a spin — handled by the laboratory workforce, medicine's largest invisible profession. The lab file.

title: Gout: The Misnamed Disease in the Modern Data
summary: Gout was caricatured as the rich man's indulgence. The modern data place it in the kidney file, the soda file, and the Black community's joints at rising rates. The gout file.

title: The Eye Doctor on the Block: Black-Owned Optometry Practices
summary: The optometry office is where the glaucoma file gets found or missed — and its ownership, in the neighborhoods that need it most, is a small-business story of its own. The optometry file.

title: Black Retirement: Social Security's Outsized Role
summary: Social Security provides half or more of income for a majority of Black retirees — the retirement system's load-bearing wall. The SSA and Census data.

title: Black Shreveport: The Red River City of North Louisiana
summary: Shreveport holds about 105,000 Black residents in the city and 145,000 across the metro — a majority-Black city on the Red River. The census profile.

title: Money Class: Financial Literacy and the Mandate Wave
summary: Half the states now require a personal-finance course to graduate — a reform aimed squarely at the wealth file — and its evidence is the rare kind that improves the longer researchers look at it. The money-class file.

title: The Railroad File: Black Workers on the Iron Road
summary: The Pullman porter was the most famous Black worker in America — and the railroad's other thousand jobs were closed to his brothers for a century. The iron road's ledger, then and now.

title: The Liver Paradox: Fat, Fire, and the Organ That Keeps Secrets
summary: Black Americans carry more diabetes and obesity yet less fatty liver in the imaging data — a genuine physiological puzzle with a darker second half. The liver file.

title: The Drafting Table: Black Architects and Their Firms
summary: Two percent of America's licensed architects are Black — and the firms they lead design, disproportionately, the churches, schools, and civic rooms of the communities in this atlas. The architecture file.

title: African Immigrants in the United States: The Fastest-Growing Black Stream
summary: About 2.4 million Black immigrants were born in Africa — the fastest-growing segment of Black America, with the highest education rates in the file. The Pew and Census data.

title: Black Montgomery: The Cradle of the Confederacy and the Capital of the Movement
summary: Montgomery holds about 125,000 Black residents in the city and 155,000 across the metro — a majority-Black capital holding both foundings. The census profile.

title: The Language Lab: Who Gets to Learn the World's Tongues
summary: The world-language classroom sorts as faithfully as the algebra track — Spanish everywhere, Mandarin and Arabic rationed, and the African languages of the diaspora's own heritage nearly absent from the catalog. The language file.

title: The Hospitality File: Black Workers in America's Hotels
summary: The hotel was once the summit of Black service work — the waiter's tuxedo economy — and is now a franchised floor of housekeepers and desk clerks under other people's flags. The hospitality ledger.

title: The Movement File: Physical Activity in the Federal Data
summary: The guidelines say 150 minutes a week. The activity data show who gets them, who works too physically to need them, and why the two kinds of movement are not the same. The movement file.

title: The Living Room: Black-Owned Coffee Shops as Civic Infrastructure
summary: The Black coffee shop sells a four-dollar drink and rents the city's best third place for free — study hall, boardroom, gallery, and salon at the price of a latte. The coffee shop file.

title: Food Insecurity in Black Households: One in Five
summary: About one in five Black households experiences food insecurity in the USDA's annual measurement — double the national rate. The food security data.

title: Black Knoxville: East Tennessee's Marble City
summary: Knoxville holds about 32,000 Black residents in the city and 52,000 across the metro — East Tennessee's largest Black community, from Beck's archive to the Sunsphere. The census profile.

title: 64 Squares: Chess and the Black Mind at Play
summary: Chess was supposed to be the meritocracy in a box — and Black players, from the Harlem clubs to the first Black grandmaster, have been proving the mind while documenting the door. The chess file.

title: Below the Line: Black Crews in Film and Television
summary: The credits roll for six minutes because the industry is a small city — and its neighborhoods, from the writers' room to the grip truck, sort by race as faithfully as any census tract. The production file.

title: The Gift File: Organ Donation in the Data
summary: The transplant file's other side: who gives. Black Americans are asked for organs more and consent less in the data — and the reasons are written in the system's own history. The gift file.

title: Wheels Up: The Black Food Truck File
summary: The food truck is the restaurant industry's lowest doorway and its hardest grind — the commissary fees, the city's permit map, and the truck-to-restaurant ladder measured in the data.

title: Getting There: Black Households, Cars, and Transit
summary: Black households are three to four times likelier to have no car — in a country built for drivers. The Census transportation and commuting data.

title: Black Lexington: Horse Country's Other Bloodlines
summary: Lexington holds about 46,000 Black residents in the city and 58,000 across the metro — home to the Black jockeys who ruled the early Derby. The census profile.

title: The Two Percent: Black Men in America's Classrooms
summary: About two of every hundred public school teachers are Black men, in classrooms where fifteen of every hundred students are Black. The smallest faculty file in the atlas.

title: The Flight Deck: Black Pilots and the Aviation Pipeline
summary: Fewer than one pilot in twenty-five is Black — in the industry the Tuskegee Airmen proved themselves in, at ruinous cost, eighty years ago. The flight deck file, from the training bill to the captain's fourth stripe.

title: The Quiet Protection: Hearing, Noise, and the Untreated Ear
summary: Black Americans show strikingly lower hearing loss in the national exams — until the factory's noise is accounted. And almost nobody, in any row, gets hearing aids. The hearing file.

title: The Agent's Office: Black-Owned Insurance Agencies
summary: The insurance agent was the debit era's pillar and the suburb's first Black professional — and the independent agency he built is now an endangered, valuable firm. The agency file.

title: Black Religion: The Church in the Data
summary: About three-quarters of Black Americans identify as Christian, and the Black church remains the community's most durable institution. The Pew religious landscape data.

title: Black Dayton: The Funk Capital's West Side
summary: Dayton holds about 58,000 Black residents in the city and 100,000 across the metro — the West Side that gave the world the Ohio Players. The census profile.

title: The Form That Opens the Door: FAFSA Completion and Black Students
summary: The federal aid form decides who can pay for college before any admissions letter arrives, and Black seniors complete it at lower rates, leaving grant money unclaimed every year. The form file.

title: The Long Haul: Black Truckers and the Owner-Operator Dream
summary: One trucker in seven is Black — in an industry whose solo owner-operator was the original small businessman of the highway, and whose freight now moves on contracts written elsewhere. The trucking file.

title: The Silent Thief: Glaucoma in the Black Population
summary: Glaucoma steals sight from the edges inward, without pain, for years — and it comes earlier, faster, and blinder for Black Americans than for any other group in the exam data. The glaucoma file.

title: The Empty Glass Ceiling: Black Brewers and Winemakers
summary: One percent of America's craft breweries are Black-owned — in an industry built on a beverage with African roots, sold to the most diverse drinking generation in history. The empty-glass file.

title: Black America by Generation: From the Silent Generation to Gen Alpha
summary: Black America's median age is about 34 — younger than the nation's — and each generation's data describe a different country. The generational profile.

title: Black Toledo: The Glass City's North End
summary: Toledo holds about 75,000 Black residents in the city and 95,000 across the metro — over a quarter of the Glass City, from Scott High's maroon to the Jeep plant. The census profile.

title: The Cafeteria Line: School Meals and the Black Student
summary: School meals are the largest nutrition program in Black children's lives, and eligibility, participation, and the universal-meals experiment all register in the federal counts. The cafeteria file.

title: The Night Watch: Black Security Guards and the Guarded Economy
summary: One security guard in four is Black — the uniform of the economy's night shift, guarding property in an industry built on low wages and the veteran's and retiree's second careers. The watch file.

title: The Empty Shelf: Food Insecurity in the Federal Measure
summary: One Black household in five is food-insecure in the USDA's own measure — a rate twice the national line, in the richest food economy in human history. The hunger file.

title: The Supermarket File: Black-Owned Grocery in the Food Desert's Economy
summary: The Black-owned supermarket is the hardest business in this section — thin margins, giant rivals, sacred purpose — the store whose survival is a neighborhood's food security. The grocery file.

title: Languages of Black America: Spanish, Creole, French, and the African Tongues
summary: About one in eight Black Americans speaks a language other than English at home. The ACS language data behind the multilingual community.

title: Black Grand Rapids: Furniture City's Southeast Side
summary: Grand Rapids holds about 38,000 Black residents in the city and 60,000 across the metro — West Michigan's largest Black community. The census profile.

title: The 529 Gap: College Savings Before College
summary: College savings accounts are opened for a small minority of Black children, so the head start that compound growth gives other families rarely starts. The savings file.

title: The Invisible Shift: Janitors and the People Who Clean the Building
summary: One building cleaner in five is Black. They arrive as the office empties, hold the keys to everything, and anchor some of the labor movement's most famous victories. The cleaning file.

title: The Untreated Ache: Chronic Pain in the Data
summary: Black Americans report more severe pain, receive less treatment for it, and were prescribed the fewest opioids in the epidemic's first wave — a file with two disasters inside one diagnosis. The pain file.

title: The Portrait Studio: Black Photographers and the Archive They Built
summary: For a century the Black portrait studio was the community's official memory — the backdrop, the props, the dignity composed — and its heirs now shoot the weddings, the brands, and the covers. The photography file.

title: Black America's Future in the Projections: Growth to Mid-Century
summary: The Census Bureau projects the Black population to keep growing through 2060, aging as it grows, on immigration and the youngest cohorts. The official projections data.

title: Black Flint: Vehicle City After the Water
summary: Flint holds about 55,000 Black residents in the city and 82,000 across the metro — a majority-Black city whose name became a warning. The census profile.

title: Ready or Not: The Kindergarten Door
summary: Children are assessed the month they meet school, and Black five-year-olds arrive with measurably less of what the assessments reward, a gap built before school begins. The readiness file.

title: The Caseworkers: Black Social Workers and the Load They Carry
summary: One social worker in five is Black — staffing the child welfare, hospital, and school systems their own communities meet most, translating the state to the family and the family to the state. The social-work file.

title: The Misnamed Pain: Migraine in Black America
summary: Migraine disables millions — and in Black patients it is more often called sinus, stress, or nothing at all. The prevalence is comparable; the diagnosis and the modern medicines are not. The migraine file.

title: The Hardware Store: Nails, Knowledge, and the Big Box's Shadow
summary: The neighborhood hardware store was the tradesman's bank, school, and supply house in one aisle — and the Black-owned store carried the contractors the big chains wouldn't credit. The hardware file.

title: Black Population Growth in the Census Record, 1790 to Today
summary: From 757,208 counted in the first census of 1790 to roughly 47 million today — the decennial record of a people's growth under slavery, freedom, migration, and return. The historical demography.

title: Black Lansing: The Capital City's South and West Sides
summary: Lansing holds about 27,000 Black residents in the city and 45,000 across the metro — Michigan's capital, an auto town, and a state-government city. The census profile.

title: The Health Room: School Nurses and Black Students
summary: One nurse per 750 students is the federal recommendation; the schools Black children attend run far thinner, and the health room is their clinic of first resort. The school nurse file.

title: Wired In: Black Electricians and the Skilled Trades
summary: Electricians earn among the highest wages in the trades, and Black workers hold under a tenth of the jobs. The electrician file, from apprenticeship intake to the electrification boom.

title: The Clouded Lens: Cataracts and the Surgery Gap
summary: Cataract is the world's leading cause of blindness and America's most curable — yet Black patients reach the operating room later, with worse vision, and lose sight to a fifteen-minute operation. The cataract file.

title: Routes and Contracts: Black-Owned Landscaping Companies
summary: Landscaping is easy to enter and hard to scale, and Black firms cluster in the residential tier while commercial contracts circulate elsewhere. The landscaping file.

title: Black Veterans: Two and a Half Million Who Served
summary: About 2.4 million Black veterans live in the United States — roughly one veteran in eight — with the highest service rates of any group among women. The demographic profile.

title: Black El Paso: The Border's Garrison and the Sun City's Small, Deep Community
summary: El Paso holds about 24,000 Black residents in the city and 29,000 across the metro — a small share of a border metropolis, built largely by Fort Bliss. The census profile.

title: The Summer That Prices the Career: Internships and Black Students
summary: Paid internships are the first rung of the professional ladder, and Black students are underrepresented in paid seats and overexposed to unpaid ones. The internship file.

title: Earn While You Learn: Black Workers and Apprenticeship
summary: Apprenticeship is the paid on-ramp to the good trades jobs, and Black workers hold a modest share of its seats. The apprenticeship file, from intake design to the completion gate.

title: The Last Address: Nursing Homes and the Segregation That Stayed
summary: America desegregated its hospitals with a signature in 1966. Its nursing homes never quite followed — the quality data still sort by the race of the residents down the hall. The last-address file.

title: Owning the Weather: Black-Owned HVAC Companies
summary: HVAC ownership rides on distributorships, trade credit, and maintenance contracts, and Black firms hold a small share of all three. The HVAC file.

title: The Black Middle Class: Half the Population, Measured in Full
summary: About half of Black households sit in the middle-income tier — around 18 million people — with an upper tier that has tripled since the 1970s. The demographic profile of the class.

title: Black Tucson: The Old Pueblo's South Side and the Air Base
summary: Tucson holds about 29,000 Black residents in the city and 46,000 across the metro — a desert community built by the railroad, the university, and Davis-Monthan. The census profile.

title: First in the Family: The First-Generation File
summary: About half of Black undergraduates are the first in their families to attend college, and the completion gap tracks a hidden curriculum, not ability. The first-generation file.

title: The Second Shift: Black Workers and Multiple Jobs
summary: About five in a hundred workers hold more than one job, and Black workers, Black women most of all, run above the line. The moonlighting file.

title: The Needle's Ledger: Vaccination in the Data
summary: Flu shots, childhood series, and the pandemic's great catch-up: the vaccination file measures a gap that closed more in three years than in thirty — and the trust research that explains both the gap and the closing.

title: The Bonded Ceiling: Black-Owned Electrical Contractors
summary: Electrical contracting adds a financial license, bonding capacity, on top of the trade license, and that second gate is where Black firms' growth is decided. The contracting file.

title: Black Interracial Marriage: One in Five New Marriages Crosses the Line
summary: About 19% of Black newlyweds marry someone of another race — up from 5% in 1980 — with a two-to-one gap between husbands and wives. The Pew and census record.

title: Black Greenville: The Upstate's Textile-and-BMW Crossroads
summary: Greenville holds about 55,000 Black residents in the city and 155,000 across the metro — the South Carolina Upstate's anchor community. The census profile.

title: The New Arena: Black Students and Esports
summary: Black teenagers game at high rates and hold a small share of school esports rosters, a new activity distributing opportunity along the oldest map. The esports file.

title: The Laptop Divide: Black Workers and Remote Work
summary: The jobs that can be done from a laptop are not the jobs Black workers mostly hold, and the newest workplace divide follows the oldest occupational lines. The remote-work file.

title: The Butterfly Gland: Thyroid Disease in Black America
summary: The thyroid's disorders split by race in the laboratory data — the underactive gland diagnosed less, the overactive more, and both masked by the two most misread complaints in medicine: tired and gaining, anxious and losing. The thyroid file.

title: Counsel and Ownership: Black-Owned Law Firms
summary: Black lawyers are about five percent of the profession and own a few percent of its offices, capturing a smaller share still of its revenue. The law firm file.

title: Black Retirement Savings: Participating at the Same Rate, Accumulating Half
summary: Black workers join 401(k) plans at rates close to white workers — then accumulate roughly half the balance. The leakage, loan, and contribution data behind the gap.

title: Black Fort Wayne: 42,000 People in the Summit City
summary: Fort Wayne's Black community, about 42,000 strong and 15% of the city, grew with the Harvester and wire plants and holds the southeast side. The census portrait.

title: Making the Case: Black Students and Debate
summary: Debate is the best-evaluated enrichment activity in the record, and its national circuit is priced like a second college fund while urban leagues rebuild its base. The debate file.

title: License to Earn: Black Plumbers and Pipefitters
summary: Plumbers and pipefitters earn above-median wages behind a license that narrows pay gaps, yet Black workers hold under a tenth of the trade. The plumbing file.

title: The Unread Skin: Psoriasis on Black Skin
summary: Psoriasis is diagnosed at half the expected rate in Black patients — not because the disease is half as present, but because the textbooks taught it in pink. The skin file's lesson in what a picture is worth.

title: Refund Season: Black-Owned Tax Preparation Firms
summary: Tax season makes the storefront preparer a central financial institution in Black neighborhoods, and Black-owned practices are built on the trust transacted at that counter. The tax file.

title: Black Broadband and Digital Access: Connected by Phone, Gapped at the Desk
summary: About 8 in 10 Black households have broadband — but Black adults are twice as likely to depend on a smartphone alone. The NTIA and Pew data on the modern access divide.

title: Black South Bend: 27,000 People in Notre Dame's Other City
summary: South Bend's Black community, about 27,000 strong and 26% of the city, built itself around Studebaker and Bendix and remade its politics. The census portrait.

title: The Student Press: Black Students and School Journalism
summary: School newspapers are dying fastest where Black students attend, and the yearbook's price decides whose archive is complete. The student press file.

title: The Refrigerant License: Black HVAC Technicians
summary: HVAC technicians are scarce, well paid, and reachable through a cheap open credential, yet Black workers hold under a tenth of the trade. The HVAC technician file.

title: The Eyes Have It Last: Vision Care and the Preventable Dark
summary: Black Americans go blind from treatable eye disease at multiples of the white rate — in a field where nearly every major cause is preventable with a pair of glasses, a drop, or a timely laser. The vision file.

title: After the Storm: Black-Owned Roofing Companies
summary: Roofing is a storm-driven, insurance-mediated industry of trust, and Black firms hold a small share of it far from the neighborhoods where they win it. The roofing file.

title: Eviction and Black Renters: The Court Date Behind the Housing Numbers
summary: Black renters — above all Black women — face America's highest eviction filing rates, in some counties a majority of all filings. The Eviction Lab and court-record data.

title: Black Springfield, Massachusetts: 33,000 People in Basketball's Birthplace
summary: Springfield's Black community, about 33,000 strong and 21% of the city, is among New England's largest — anchored in Mason Square for a century. The census portrait.

title: Opening Night: Black Students and School Theatre
summary: Theatre is the least universal school art, its availability steepest down the poverty gradient, and its backstage pipeline among entertainment's least diverse. The theatre file.

title: Framing the Country: Black Carpenters
summary: Carpentry is construction's largest trade and one of its most cyclical, and Black carpenters hold under a tenth of its jobs across two very different labor markets. The carpenter file.

title: The Crown File: Black Women and Scarring Hair Loss
summary: The most common scarring hair loss in Black women was studied late, is diagnosed later, and destroys follicles while it waits. The alopecia file.

title: Sunlight and Ownership: Black-Owned Solar Installers
summary: Solar is a policy-built industry whose workforce and ownership demographics report on who policy reaches, and Black firms hold a small share of its young market. The solar file.

title: Black Single Fathers: The Fastest-Growing Household Nobody Counts First
summary: Roughly 570,000 Black fathers raise children alone — a population that has grown for five decades and outperforms its stereotype in the outcome data. The census profile.

title: Black Worcester: 27,000 People in the Heart of the Commonwealth
summary: Worcester's Black community, about 27,000 strong and 13% of the city, grew with the wire mills and anchors today's eds-and-meds economy. The census portrait.

title: The Strings File: Black Students and the Orchestra
summary: Black musicians are under two percent of U.S. orchestra rosters, the integral of a pipeline that begins with a rented quarter-size violin. The strings file.

title: The Fair Test: Black Welders
summary: Welding certifies skill by breaking the evidence, the fairest audition in the trades, and Black welders hold about a tenth of the work, concentrated on the Gulf. The welder file.

title: The Interrupted Night: Black Adults and Sleep Apnea
summary: Black adults carry sleep apnea at elevated rates and are diagnosed later and less often, while its untreated years multiply the chronic disease burden. The apnea file.

title: Trusted With the Family: Black-Owned Pet Services
summary: The pet economy's service end runs on trust and clipper craft, and Black groomers and kennel owners are building a growing share of it. The pet services file.

title: Multigenerational Households: A Quarter of Black America Lives Three Generations Deep
summary: About 26% of Black Americans live in multigenerational households — a living arrangement that is economic strategy, care system, and the data's rebuttal to the nuclear norm.

title: Black New Haven: 42,000 People in the Elm City
summary: New Haven's Black community, about 42,000 strong and 31% of the city, is among Connecticut's largest — rooted in Dixwell Avenue's century of institutions. The census portrait.

title: Choice's Bargain: Black Students and Magnet Schools
summary: Magnets were built to make integration attractive and now ration quality through lotteries, auditions, and bus routes that Black families navigate heavily. The magnet file.

title: Under the Hood: Black Auto Technicians
summary: Auto technicians hold the strongest Black share in the trades, concentrated in fleets and independent shops, as the electric transition rewrites the skill base. The mechanic file.

title: Found Earlier: Black Children and Autism Diagnosis
summary: Autism identification for Black children finally converged with white children's in federal surveillance, after decades of later diagnosis. The autism file.

title: The Tunnel and the Hand: Black-Owned Car Washes
summary: The subscription tunnel reinvented the car wash, deleting the crew jobs and raising entry capital, while Black owners hold the detailing and legacy segments. The car wash file.

title: Black Population by Region: The South Holds the Majority Again
summary: About 57% of Black Americans live in the South — a majority restored after a century of dispersal. The regional distribution data, and the flows still running.

title: Black Bridgeport: 52,000 People in Connecticut's Largest City
summary: Bridgeport's Black community, about 52,000 strong and 35% of the city, is Connecticut's biggest — built on the East End's factory century. The census portrait.

title: The Shadow System: Black Students and Tutoring
summary: Private tutoring converts income into advantage at rates Black families access least, while public high-dosage tutoring became the era's best-proven remedy. The tutoring file.

title: The Default Eye: Black Graphic Designers
summary: Design hires by portfolio, yet Black designers hold a small share of jobs and a smaller share of creative direction, in a field whose product is audience judgment. The design file.

title: The Matching Problem: Black Donors and the Blood Supply
summary: The blood that sickle cell patients need most can only reliably come from Black donors, who are a small fraction of the donor pool. The blood file.

title: The Strip-Mall Conservatory: Black-Owned Dance Studios
summary: Black-owned dance studios are the strip-mall conservatories of Black America, durable women-owned businesses negotiating ballet's closed door and majorette's open one. The dance studio file.

title: Black Household Debt: Less of It, Heavier to Carry
summary: Black households carry less total debt than the national average — and more of it in the expensive kinds, against lower incomes. The Federal Reserve's debt file.

title: Black Akron: 59,000 People in the Rubber Capital
summary: Akron's Black community, about 59,000 strong and 31% of the city, was built by the tire plants and carries one of Ohio's deepest Black civic records. The census portrait.

title: The Pyramid: Black Students and Science Research
summary: Science competitions narrow from a universal school fair to a laboratory-resourced national stage, and Black finalists measure in the low single digits. The science fair file.

title: Hands That Heal: Black Physical Therapists
summary: Physical therapy's doctoral door lifted its wages and narrowed its workforce, leaving Black therapists at about one in twenty in clinics full of Black patients. The PT file.

title: The Two-Tier Visit: Black Patients and Telehealth
summary: Black patients use telehealth heavily but through its thinnest channel, the audio-only call, in a divide written by broadband, portals, and privacy. The telehealth file.

title: Judgment by the Hour: Black-Owned Consulting Firms
summary: Black-owned consultancies sell judgment to governments and corporations in the niches the giants underserve, against a past-performance ledger that gates the first anchor client. The consulting file.

title: Unbanked Households: One in Nine Black Households Outside the Banking System
summary: About 11% of Black households have no bank account at all — five times the white rate — and a third are underbanked. The FDIC's biennial file.

title: Black Youngstown: 26,000 People in the City That Named Deindustrialization
summary: Youngstown's Black community, about 26,000 and 44% of the city, lived the steel collapse that made the city's name an economics term — and runs the city that remains.

title: The Redistributed Summer: Black Students and the School Calendar
summary: Balanced calendars concentrate in the urban districts Black students attend, carrying modest average effects and the strongest equity rationale in the time file. The calendar file.

title: The Preventive Chair: Black Dental Hygienists
summary: A two-year licensed profession in chronic shortage holds one of allied health's thinnest Black shares, throttled by awareness and advising rather than barriers. The hygienist file.

title: The Missed Diagnosis: Black Women and PCOS
summary: PCOS affects about one in ten women, multiplies diabetes risk, and is diagnosed latest in Black women, whose presentation the criteria fit worst. The PCOS file.

title: The Reel Is the Resume: Black-Owned Videography Companies
summary: Videography's portfolio is public and its craft is auditable, and Black production companies climb from weddings and church media toward owned libraries. The videography file.

title: Life Insurance: The One Policy Black Households Buy at Higher Rates
summary: Black adults own life insurance at rates equal to or above the national average — a century-old protection culture the industry data record, with a coverage-amount gap inside it.

title: Black Harrisburg: 26,000 People in a Majority-Black State Capital
summary: Harrisburg's Black community, about 26,000 and a majority of Pennsylvania's capital city, governs a capital from neighborhoods a freeway was driven through. The census portrait.

title: The Revolving Door: Keeping Black Teachers
summary: Black teachers leave at higher rates under loads the workload accounting never counts, and the cost compounds across every student they would have taught. The retention file.

title: The Voice in the Headset: Black Air Traffic Controllers
summary: Fewer than fifteen thousand controllers move America's air traffic through one of its most audited hiring funnels, and Black controllers hold about a tenth of the seats. The controller file.

title: The Stranded Third: Black Americans and Epilepsy
summary: Epilepsy is common and usually controllable, but the specialty pathway, monitoring units and surgery, reaches Black patients late and least. The epilepsy file.

title: Names in Light: Black-Owned Sign Companies
summary: Sign shops design, fabricate, and permit the names above every door, and Black shops inherit the hand-painted tradition in a business whose portfolio hangs in public. The sign file.

title: Afro-Latino Americans: Six Million People at the Census's Crossroads
summary: About 6 million Afro-Latinos live in the U.S. — counted inside both the Black and Hispanic totals, fully visible in neither. The Pew and Census data on the overlap.

title: Black Erie: 16,000 People on the Lake
summary: Erie's Black community, about 16,000 and 17% of Pennsylvania's lakefront city, was built by the lake trade and the plants — and holds the city's east side through its reinvention.

title: The Last Gate: Black Students and Calculus
summary: Calculus is decided in eighth grade, by placement systems that sort equally scored Black students downward, and the gate guards the STEM majors beyond it. The calculus file.

title: Keepers of the Collection: Black Librarians
summary: The library promises equal access through a master's-gated workforce that is five percent Black, above a diverse support tier doing the same public work. The librarian file.

title: The Last Mile: Black Women and Cervical Cancer
summary: A nearly eliminable cancer persists in specific counties and populations: screening converged, but follow-up after abnormal results did not. The cervical file.

title: Two Ledgers: Black-Owned Liquor Stores
summary: Liquor retail is rationed by license, making entry a capital purchase, and its density map binds the business ledger to the health ledger in one storefront. The liquor file.

title: The Energy Burden: Black Households Pay More of Their Income to Keep the Lights On
summary: Black households carry an energy burden roughly 40-60% higher than the national median in the ACEEE analyses — paying more, per dollar of income, for the same warmth and light. The household data.

title: Black Beaumont: 55,000 People in the Golden Triangle
summary: Beaumont's Black community, about 55,000 and nearly half the city, was built by Spindletop's oil and the refinery corridor — and anchors Texas's Golden Triangle. The census portrait.

title: The Unfinished Experiment: Black Children and Head Start
summary: Head Start enrolls Black children at double their population share, rations seats to half the eligible, and produces life outcomes its test scores understate. The Head Start file.

title: The Engine Room: Black Paralegals
summary: Paralegals are the legal system's representative workforce behind a profession that is not, and the licensing experiments may convert them into independent practitioners. The paralegal file.

title: Counting the Weight: Black Adults and Anxiety
summary: Measured anxiety prevalence runs lower among Black adults while severity and untreated duration run higher, a paradox of supports, stigma, and symptom dialects. The anxiety file.

title: The Worst Hour: Black-Owned Towing Companies
summary: Towing is a dispatch economy gated by police rotations and motor club algorithms, where reputation at a customer's worst hour is the Black firm's durable asset. The towing file.

title: The Mississippi Delta: The Blackest Region in America, County by County
summary: Across the Delta's river counties, Black majorities of 60-80% govern the poorest ground in the nation — and its richest cultural soil. The regional data portrait.

title: Black Pine Bluff: 31,000 People in One of America's Blackest Cities
summary: Pine Bluff's Black community, about 31,000 and three-quarters of the city, holds an HBCU, a Delta farming heritage, and one of the starkest decline-and-endurance files in the South. The census portrait.

title: The Test and the Practice: Black Students and Civics
summary: A quarter of Black eighth graders test proficient in civics while their communities post the nation's densest civic life: the test and the practice are different files. The civics file.

title: Breathing for Others: Black Respiratory Therapists
summary: An associate-degree license reaches the ICU's ventilators, and respiratory therapy's Black share is among allied health's strongest. The respiratory file.

title: Back, Firm, Flat, Alone: Black Infants and Safe Sleep
summary: Back-sleeping cut infant deaths dramatically, but the Black rate remains roughly double, in a gap written by housing, leave, and grandmothers' authority. The safe sleep file.

title: The Gatehouse: Black-Owned Real Estate Brokerages
summary: Black brokers navigate the housing market's documented disparities for their buyers, making the Black-owned brokerage both a business and fair housing infrastructure. The brokerage file.

title: Black Appalachia: A Million People the Mountain Story Forgot to Count
summary: Appalachia's Black residents — coal miners' grandchildren, steel families, and the Affrilachian poets — number near a million across the region's counties. The data portrait.

title: Black Trenton: 44,000 in the Capital City New Jersey Walks Past
summary: Trenton's Black community, roughly 44,000 and half the capital, governs a city the state works in and leaves — the Making and remaking files in one ledger. The census portrait.

title: The Course That Left the Building: Black Students and Driver Education
summary: Driver ed left the public school for the strip mall, repricing the license's first step onto the family budget, with the toll falling where the license matters most. The driver ed file.

title: The Credentialed Eye: Black Radiologic Technologists
summary: Imaging technologists produce the pictures diagnosis rides on, face a repricing shortage, and thin toward the summit specialties. The imaging file.

title: Fifteen Minutes a Year: Black Children and Well-Child Visits
summary: Well-child attendance starts high and decays fastest for Black children into adolescence, bundling a dozen missed screenings behind one appointment. The well-child file.

title: The Leasing Office: Black-Owned Property Management
summary: Property management is real estate's subscription business, and Black firms hold the affordable housing specialty where compliance is the moat. The management file.

title: The Inheritance Gap: The Wealth That Arrives by Envelope
summary: White families receive inheritances at roughly twice the Black rate, in amounts several times larger — the transfer system's quiet compounding in the Federal Reserve data.

title: Black Killeen: 60,000 in the City the Army Built
summary: Killeen's Black community, roughly 60,000 and over a third of the city, is Fort Cavazos made civilian — the military pipeline's hometown, with its economics in uniform. The census portrait.

title: The Locked Gate: Black Children, Swimming, and Survival
summary: Black children drown at multiples of the white rate because the lesson was segregated two generations ago; ten lessons cut the risk nearly ninety percent. The water file.

title: First Hands: Black EMTs and Paramedics
summary: EMS is licensed health care's most representative workforce and its worst-paid license, staffing the street-level front door of every disparity in the health files. The EMS file.

title: Ten Degrees Apart: Black Americans and Heat
summary: The hottest neighborhoods in American cities are the ones drawn for Black residence, and heat is becoming a health statistic with a map. The heat file.

title: The Discipline Economy: Black-Owned Martial Arts Studios
summary: Black martial arts schools run a tuition annuity selling discipline and safety, rooted in a lineage of urban masters who built the authority themselves. The martial arts file.

title: Black Marriage in the Data: Rates, Timing, and the Economics Beneath Them
summary: About a third of Black adults are married today, down from two-thirds in 1960 — a trend the data tie to wages, the removal of men from their communities, and women's rising education. The marriage file.

title: Black Eatonville: 2,300 People in the Oldest Black Town in America
summary: Incorporated in 1887 and immortalized by Zora Neale Hurston, Eatonville still governs itself — a small town carrying an outsized share of the record. The census portrait.

title: The Shortcut, Audited: Black Students and Coding Bootcamps
summary: Bootcamps enrolled Black students at population share and placed them behind the cohort, the shortcut's risks distributed by the wealth file. The bootcamp file.

title: The First Voice: Black 911 Dispatchers
summary: Dispatchers, heavily Black in the urban centers, perform blind triage classified as clerical work, and their coaching voices are a measured survival variable. The dispatch file.

title: The Bathroom Door at 2 A.M.: Falls and Older Black Adults
summary: Falls assemble from the atlas's other conditions meeting a deferred-maintenance house, and the repair is sometimes a thirty-dollar grab bar. The falls file.

title: The Homecoming Fleet: Black-Owned Charter Bus Companies
summary: Charter buses carry Black America's collective calendar, and the Black carriers who own them cleared a half-million-dollar gate one coach at a time. The charter file.

title: The Black Intermountain West: Small Numbers, Fast Growth, Long Roots
summary: Utah, Idaho, Montana, and Wyoming hold some of America's smallest Black populations — and some of its fastest growth rates, on roots older than the states themselves. The regional portrait.

title: Black Mound Bayou: 1,400 People in the Town Freedom Built for Itself
summary: Founded in 1887 by men born enslaved, Mound Bayou remains almost entirely Black — a Delta town whose hospital, bank, and oil mill wrote a century's proof of concept. The census portrait.

title: The Runway: Black Students and Aviation Academies
summary: Black students are thirty percent of aviation academies and three percent of airline pilots: the academies are the down payment on the flight deck's slow turning. The aviation file.

title: The Mapmakers: Black Urban Planners
summary: The profession that drew the segregated map is five percent Black, and its planners now staff the repair, translating neighborhood knowledge into the plan's language. The planning file.

title: Written in Contrast: Black Patients and Vitiligo
summary: Vitiligo is clinically benign and psychologically heavy, heaviest on the deepest skin, while its treatments ration by schedule and specialty access. The vitiligo file.

title: Paid to Wait: Black-Owned Self-Storage
summary: Self-storage is real estate's quietest fortune, and Black owners hold corridor land in its independent tier, paid monthly to wait. The storage file.

title: The Passport Gap: Who Holds the Little Blue Book
summary: Roughly half of Americans hold passports; Black Americans hold them at lower rates — and the travel data show a generation closing the gap on its own terms. The passport file.

title: Black Prince George's County: The Wealthiest Majority-Black County in America
summary: Nearly a million people, almost two-thirds Black, with a median household income rivaling rich suburbs everywhere — Prince George's County is the suburban file's Exhibit A. The data portrait.

title: The Second System: Black Students and Music Education
summary: The heirs of American music attend schools with the thinnest music staffing, while the church and the marching band run a rigorous parallel system. The music file.

title: The Night Economy: Black Workers and Shift Schedules
summary: One in five Black workers works nights, evenings, or rotating shifts, staffing the infrastructure the daylight is built on. The night file.

title: The Front Door: Black Patients and Primary Care
summary: A usual source of care predicts nearly everything else in the health files, and Black adults hold it less often, in clinics rather than offices. The primary care file.

title: Keeping It Rolling: Black-Owned Tire Shops
summary: The independent tire dealer admitted Black capital when franchises would not, and the shop that carried the neighborhood to payday still anchors its corridor. The tire file.

title: The Homegoing Ledger: Burial, Cremation, and the Economics of the Last Ceremony
summary: America now cremates more than it buries — but Black families still choose burial at far higher rates, and the funeral data record both a theology and an industry in transition. The homegoing file.

title: Black Gary: 53,000 People in the City Steel Built and Left
summary: Founded by U.S. Steel in 1906, Gary drew generations to the mills — and became a majority-Black city just as the industry's collapse arrived. The census portrait.

title: The Shadow Faculty: Black Students and Arts Education
summary: The arts are rationed by the funding gradient and then supplied by a shadow faculty that is itself underfunded at fractions per participant. The arts file.

title: Too Much or Not Enough: Black Workers' Hours
summary: The average week conceals a split: hours rationed at the bottom, tournament hours at the top, and the standard forty thinning between. The hours file.

title: Ten Years Is Not a Phase: Black Women and Menopause
summary: Black women's menopause starts earlier, burns longer, and is treated least, a decade of symptoms the clinical system files as a phase. The menopause file.

title: Fuel and Refuge: Black-Owned Gas Stations
summary: The Black-owned station was Green Book infrastructure, thinned by self-service and tank regulation, now standing where the charging map will be drawn. The station file.

title: Uncoupling: Divorce, Separation, and Remarriage in the Black Data
summary: Black marriages end at higher rates, separations last longer, and remarriage comes slower in the data — a file about what breaks, what lingers, and what the numbers miss.

title: Black Benton Harbor: 8,000 People Across the River From Another America
summary: Benton Harbor and St. Joseph share a river, a bridge, and a metro area — and almost nothing else in the data. A paired-city portrait of America's closest stark divide.

title: Roots as a Technology: Grow-Your-Own Teacher Pipelines
summary: The district that grows its own teachers recruits more Black and keeps them longer, on the theory that rootedness is instructional capital. The grow-your-own file.

title: The Seam: Black Workers in Mining
summary: Black miners built the coal camps, the union's imperfect shelter, and the pensioner towns the energy transition is leaving last. The mining file.

title: Difference or Disorder: Black Children and Speech-Language
summary: Speech evaluations must distinguish dialect from disorder, a judgment call made by a scarce, thinly diverse workforce over the root system of literacy. The speech file.

title: The License as Capital: Black-Owned Plumbing Companies
summary: The master's license made ownership the trades career's natural terminus, and the lead-line replacement wave is landing on the Black firm's home ground. The plumbing file.

title: The Adoption File: Waiting Children, Willing Families, and a System Between Them
summary: Black children wait longest for adoption in the federal foster-care data — while Black families adopt at strong rates and are recruited least. The adoption file.

title: Black DeKalb County: 410,000 People on Atlanta's East Side
summary: DeKalb is one of the three or four largest Black county populations in America — suburban, governed, and layered with history from Scottdale's mill to South DeKalb's cul-de-sacs.

title: The Hospital as Campus: Health Careers Academies
summary: The hospital becomes a campus, the graduate leaves certified, and the system grows its own workforce from the neighborhood's sixteen-year-olds. The health academy file.

title: Both Ledgers: Black Workers in Oil and Gas
summary: A tenth of the industry, craft-heavy and office-light, holding both ledgers of the fence-line bargain across three Gulf generations. The oil and gas file.

title: The Fourth Trimester: Black Mothers After Birth
summary: The postpartum year carries a large share of maternal deaths and the next thirty years' forecasts, and it was covered for sixty days until the recent extensions. The postpartum file.

title: The Stamp: Black-Owned Engineering Firms
summary: The engineer's stamp is legally identical in every hand, and the Black firms holding it design the water and transit systems of their own communities. The engineering file.

title: The Language File: African American English in the Data
summary: The most studied dialect in American linguistics is also a variable in the education, housing, and employment data — measured in test scores, callbacks, and voice recognition error rates.

title: Black Macon: 82,000 People in the Heart of Georgia
summary: Macon sits at Georgia's exact crossroads — a majority-Black city of music legends and medical centers, where the Ocmulgee's ancient banks meet the fall line's modern data.

title: Two Summers: Black Children and Summer Camp
summary: Five percent of the sleepaway campers and all of the day camp's necessity: two summers, divided by the campership, the gear, and the bus. The camp file.

title: Won as It Vanished: Black Workers in Textiles and Apparel
